people.name: Daniel Bedingfield
people.description: New Zealand-British singer and songwriter Daniel Bedingfield released his debut studio album, Gotta Get thru This, in 2002. The album generated three UK No. 1 singles: "Gotta Get thru This", "If You're Not the One", and "Never Gonna Leave Your Side".

people.name: Montell Jordan
people.description: Montell Jordan is an American R&B singer, songwriter, and producer known for his 1995 single 'This Is How We Do It', which reached No.1 in the US and No.11 in the UK.

people.name: Duane Roland
people.description: Duane Roland was a guitarist for the American Southern rock and hard rock band Molly Hatchet, known for the 1980 album 'Beatin' The Odds' and their hit song 'Flirtin' with Disaster'.

people.name: Don Barnes
people.description: Don Barnes is an American rock vocalist and guitarist and one of the founding members of the Southern rock band 38 Special.

people.name: Mike Stock
people.description: Mike Stock is an English songwriter, record producer, and musician. Through his work with the songwriting and production trio Stock Aitken Waterman, he has helped create more than a hundred top-40 hits in the UK, featuring 16 No.1s, and holds recognition from the Guinness World Records as one of the most successful songwriters in history. The trio received three Ivor Novello Awards in 1990 for Songwriter of the Year, Most Performed Work for 'This Time I Know It's for Real' by Donna Summer, and Best Selling A-Side for 'Too Many Broken Hearts' by Jason Donovan.

people.name: Nicky Stevens
people.description: Nicky Stevens is an English singer who performs with the pop group Brotherhood of Man. In 1976, the group released the hit 'Save Your Kisses for Me', which served as the United Kingdom's entry in the Eurovision Song Contest 1976. The track achieved worldwide success by climbing to No. 1 across numerous nations, such as the UK, where it finished the year as the highest-selling single.

people.name: Kimberley Rew
people.description: Kimberley Rew is a member of the British-American rock band Katrina And The Waves, which achieved widespread recognition for the 1985 hit single 'Walking on Sunshine'. Additionally, the band secured victory at the 1997 Eurovision Song Contest with their song 'Love Shine a Light'.

people.name: Mickey Thomas
people.description: American rock singer Mickey Thomas is widely recognized as a lead vocalist for Jefferson Starship and Starship, groups associated with the 1987 UK and US No. 1 hit single 'Nothing's Gonna Stop Us'. Before his time with Jefferson Starship, he performed as a backing and occasional lead singer in Elvin Bishop's band. Additionally, he served as the lead vocalist on Bishop's most famous track, 'Fooled Around And Fell In Love'.

people.name: John Wilson
people.description: John Wilson is a drummer who played in the Irish rock and blues band Taste. Taste released the 1970 UK No.18 album 'On The Boards', and the group was founded by the musician and songwriter Rory Gallagher.

people.name: Ozzy Osbourne
people.description: Ozzy Osbourne (John Michael Osbourne), singer and songwriter with English rock band Black Sabbath who had the 1970 UK No.4 single 'Paranoid'. The band's self-titled 1970 album was voted as the best British rock album ever by Kerrang! in 2005. He performed on the band's first eight studio albums before he was fired in 1979 due to his problems with drugs and alcohol. He had the 1986 solo UK No.20 single 'Shot In The Dark' and became the star of The Osbournes MTV show, which first aired in 2002. Osbourne sold over 100 million albums, including his solo work and Black Sabbath releases. Osbourne courted controversy throughout his career. He adopted the title "Prince of Darkness", took on a demonic stage persona, and portrayed himself as the "Madman of Rock". He died on 22 July 2025 at the age of 76, just seventeen days after his final live performance with Black Sabbath at the Back to the Beginning farewell concert.

people.name: Vic Malcolm
people.description: British rock band Geordie featured guitarist Vic Malcolm and singer Brian Johnson during the group's initial 1970s activity, which included notable tracks like 'Don't Do That', 'All Because of You', 'Can You Do It', 'Electric Lady', and 'Goodbye Love'. Following the February 1980 death of AC/DC frontman Bon Scott, AC/DC selected Brian Johnson to assume lead vocal responsibilities.

people.name: Ralph McTell
people.description: English singer-songwriter and guitar player Ralph McTell is best known for his 1975 UK No.2 single 'Streets of London', which has been covered by over two hundred artists worldwide. During the 1980s, he composed and performed music for two children's television programmes, starting with Alphabet Zoo and subsequently Tickle on the Tum.

people.name: Ken Lewis
people.description: Ken Lewis was a member of the English vocal trio Ivy League, who achieved their highest recognition for the 1965 UK No.3 single 'Tossing and Turning'. Earlier, in November 1964, the group provided background vocals on the hit single 'I Can't Explain' by The Who.

people.name: Andy Williams
people.description: Andy Williams was an American singer and television host who achieved the 1957 US and UK No.1 single 'Butterfly', the 1963 US and UK No.2 single 'Can't Get Used To Losing You', and more than 25 additional US Top 40 singles. He hosted the long-running Andy Williams TV show between 1962 and 1971 and accumulated worldwide sales of over 100 million records. At the age of 84, he passed away from bladder cancer on September 25th, 2012.

works.title: Out Of Sight
works.eventDescription: American drummer Melvin Parker died. He and his brother, saxophonist Maceo Parker, were key members of James Brown's band. Parker was the drummer on three of Brown's recordings: ‘Out of Sight,’ ‘Papa's Got A Brand New Bag,’ and ‘I Got You (I Feel Good).’

works.title: The Liquidator
works.eventDescription: Gladstone Anderson, a Jamaican pianist, keyboard player, and singer also known as "Gladdy," passed away at the age of 81. He contributed significantly to Jamaica's musical history by helping shape the ska sound and the rocksteady beat. Aside from performing on hundreds of recordings, he led Gladdy's All Stars, the group behind the instrumental hit "The Liquidator," which charted in 1969 and 1980.

works.title: Patience
works.eventDescription: For the first time in their career, the reunited Take That claimed the top spot on the UK singles and album charts at the same time. While their new album Beautiful World debuted at No.1, the single 'Patience' held the number one position for a second consecutive week.

works.title: Oh, Pretty Woman
works.eventDescription: American session guitarist Grady Martin passed away at the age of 72. As part of the renowned Nashville A-Team, his guitar work featured on major hits including Marty Robbins' 'El Paso', Loretta Lynn's 'Coal Miner's Daughter', and Roy Orbison's 'Oh, Pretty Woman'. Spanning a 50-year career, Martin performed as a backing musician for artists such as Woody Guthrie, Arlo Guthrie, Joan Baez, J. J. Cale, Elvis Presley, Buddy Holly, Johnny Cash, and Patsy Cline.

works.eventDescription: Boyz II Men succeeded themselves at the top of the US singles chart as 'On Bended Knee' commenced a six-week tenure at No. 1. Previously, the group held the top position for a record-setting 14 weeks with 'I'll Make Love To You'.

works.title: Better by You Better Than Me
works.eventDescription: Two families filed a lawsuit against Judas Priest, claiming the band was to blame for their sons forming a suicide pact and shooting themselves subsequent to listening to Judas Priest records. The legal representatives and parents alleged that the Judas Priest track Better By You, Better Than Me from the Stained Class album contained a subliminal message of 'do it', which they claimed incited the suicide attempt. The court proceedings ran from 16 July until 24 August 1990, resulting in the dismissal of the lawsuit.

works.title: Mull of Kintyre
works.eventDescription: Wings began a nine-week reign at No. 1 on the UK charts with 'Mull Of Kintyre'. This track became the initial single to surpass 2 million copies sold in the UK and was co-written by Denny Laine, who parted with his rights to the song during a period of bankruptcy.

works.title: Animals
works.eventDescription: Algie, a 40-foot inflatable pig, drifted into the sky above London, England, after coming loose from its moorings during a photo shoot for the upcoming Pink Floyd album Animals. A warning for pilots was issued regarding the loose flying pig by the Civil Aviation Authority. The pig ultimately landed in a barn located in Godmersham, Kent, prompting a local farmer to complain that his cows had been frightened by the event.

works.title: Brown Sugar
works.eventDescription: Over the course of three days of recording sessions at Muscle Shoals studios, the Rolling Stones recorded 'Brown Sugar'. Mick Jagger wrote the track with Marsha Hunt in mind, who was his secret girlfriend and the mother of his first child, Karis. Legal disputes with the group's previous record label delayed the release of the song for over a year. The single reached No.1 in the United States and Canada, and secured the No.2 position on the charts in the United Kingdom and Ireland.

works.title: Winchester Cathedral
works.eventDescription: British group The New Vaudeville Band began a three-week duration at the top of the US singles chart featuring 'Winchester Cathedral', which achieved a No.4 position in the UK.

works.title: Rubber Soul
works.eventDescription: The Beatles sixth studio album Rubber Soul was released. Often referred to as a folk rock album, Rubber Soul incorporates a mix of pop, soul and folk musical styles. The title derives from the colloquialism "plastic soul", which referred to soul played by English musicians. Most of the songs on the album were composed soon after the Beatles' return to London following their August 1965 North American tour. The album reflects the influence of their month in America, where they set a new attendance record when they played to over 55,000 at Shea Stadium on 15 August, met Bob Dylan in New York and their longtime hero Elvis Presley in Los Angeles.

works.title: My Generation
works.eventDescription: The debut studio album by The Who was issued in the UK as My Generation. Decca Records subsequently distributed the record in the United States in April 1966 under the title The Who Sings My Generation, featuring a distinct cover and a somewhat modified track list. Mojo magazine ranked the album as the second greatest guitar album of all time in 2003.

works.title: Little Red Rooster
works.eventDescription: Their cover of 'Little Red Rooster' gave the Rolling Stones their second No.1 single in the UK. The band recorded the track in Chicago at Chess Studios, the location where Muddy Waters, Howlin' Wolf, and Little Walter had previously cut their blues hits.

works.title: Singing the Blues
works.eventDescription: Guy Mitchell secured the No. 1 position on the US singles chart with his rendition of 'Singing The Blues', maintaining the top spot for a duration of nine weeks. Nearly concurrently with Mitchell's recording, two alternative charting versions of the track appeared: one performed by the UK vocalist Tommy Steele, accompanied by the Steelmen, and another by the US country artist Marty Robbins.

works.title: Mystery Train
works.eventDescription: Elvis Presley's debut release through RCA Victor Records was publicized, featuring the tracks 'Mystery Train' and 'I Forgot to Remember to Forget' which were acquired from Sam Phillips at Sun Records. His new label characterized him as 'The most talked about personality in recorded music in the last 10 years.'
